_comment_tools.main: R2.1. `gathered_with` on a resource names the tool id that gathers it at full amount; a resource with no `gathered_with` (berries) is never tool-gated. item_db.gd's harvest_yield() reads it: the right tool gives the harvest node's full amount, no tool gives a reduced bare-handed amount (BAREHANDED_FRACTION, tunable), and owning some other tool but not the right one gives nothing. Tools themselves are `kind: tool`, `stack: 1` â€” owned, not consumed. `hammer` and `fishing_rod` exist as items now per this task's own brief but gate nothing yet: the workbench/repair loop (R2.2) and fishing (unscheduled -- R7.6 was re-scoped off fishing and onto the berry farm) are what will read them. R7.6 added a sixth tool, `hoe`, and it is the first one that does NOT appear here: it gates TILLING, a preparation verb, not a gather, so it is named by scripts/world/farm_logic.gd::TILL_TOOL instead of by any resource's `gathered_with`. Berries are still the resource with no `gathered_with`, farmed ones included -- see docs/decisions/D50 for why that was kept deliberately rather than quietly changed the moment berries got a farm.

_comment_ironwood.main: SF31. MEADOWS_PROGRESSION_SPEC.md Â§3 Band 4 and Â§10: the SECOND and LAST of the Meadows' two progression-tier materials, above baseline wood/stone/fiber/berries and alongside Rootstone. `gathered_with: axe` because it is wood -- the spec's own note that it 'does not need to literally be iron' cuts both ways, and giving a hardwood a new gathering verb would be a mechanic where the spec asked for a tier. `kind: resource`, same as Rootstone, so no new code path. Where it grows is `data/config/harvest.json`'s `ironwood` nodes (the old-growth stands on the Rise's south-west flank, spec Band 4's 'old-growth forest'); what it buys is `data/recipes/recipes_ironwood.json`, and that file's own header holds the rule this tier is judged by: nothing the stronghold needs may require a THIRD new material.

_comment_sigils.main: SF34, spec Â§3 Band 4. Three physical items, one per regional captain, each granted through that captain's `reward` block in data/config/trainers.json. `kind: key` and `stack: 1`, exactly like `south_bridge_key` -- they are gate items, and the gate is SB10's `item_gate.gd` requiring all three at once, not a level check and not a UI lock. There is no fourth sigil and no way to buy, craft or find one: beating the captain IS the acquisition.

_comment_saddle.main: R6.2. ONE generic saddle for every mount, never a saddle per species â€” the backlog brief's own words, 'a generic saddle ... and no species-specific saddle clutter'. Which creature it fits is the CREATURE's business (species.json's `rideable.requires_item`), so a second mount at R8.5 either wants this same saddle or names its own tack there, and either way nothing changes here. `kind: gear` rather than `material`: it is a thing you own and use, like an orb, not a thing you spend. It is never consumed by riding and there is no durability on it â€” `scripts/world/riding_controller.gd::_has_tack()` only ever ASKS whether one is in the satchel. Icon deliberately points at `saddle_frame.png`: the frame is what a saddle is built on and the silhouette is right, and CLAUDE.md's asset rules say to source coherently rather than mint a near-duplicate icon for the sake of a distinct filename. A dedicated icon is a clean later swap in this one line. [Moved out of the `items` object: every other entry in there is an item dictionary, and tests/test_item_icons.gd casts each one, so a bare string inside it threw a cast error on three separate tests. Top level is where every other _comment in this file already sits.]

main.why: Behind the alpha Galecrest pack of three at (-25,7255) -- the encounter contract's 'danger beat', the largest aggressive cluster in the chapter: a Great guarded by the band's hardest ordinary fight. N14-ROUTED-FOLLOWUPS moved this coordinate on 2026-09-05, from N02-VEGETATION's routed finding Â§7: the authored spot sat inside solid scatter and `band_pickups.gd`'s nudge search could not find clear ground for it, so the world warned `sits inside solid scatter... move it` on every boot. The new coordinate is MEASURED, not guessed -- `tools/_probe_n14_pickup_ground.gd` asked the same `vegetation.gd::has_solid_scatter_near` query the placer uses over a 0.5m grid around the authored spot and reported the nearest genuinely clear cell. The place this find is about is unchanged; only the metre or so it stands on moved. Nearest clear ground was 0.5m out -- the nudge search's smallest ring is 2.0m, so it stepped straight over half a metre of clear ground and then ran out of rings.
